blocks.html: How we read the brief. The reader is a stranger who is tied to another supplier's contract. They do not think about energy, and they hang up on energy callers. So each piece starts with something the owner recognises from their own business, then shows what SGB does about it, then asks for one small step.

sections.lede: The job: make an owner who does not know SGB want to find out what SGB would cost them.

blocks.html: SGB has no brand guide yet, so the voice is built from the two sources the brief names: SGB's own lines and the 13 customer quotes. Short sentences. First and second person. Concrete things from the owner's day. No exclamation marks, no energy jargon, no promise we cannot prove.

head: Our word
Where it comes from in SGB
What it does in the copy
rows: Calm
SGB's line “STARKE TARIFE. ENTSPANNTE ENTSCHEIDUNGEN.” (relaxed decisions). Tobias Averbeck: “Whoever has secure energy and secure costs is halfway there in running the operation.” (translated)
Nothing is urgent, nothing shouts. The advisor has the date, so the owner can stop thinking about it.
Personal

SGB's pillar “PERSÖNLICHE BERATUNG”. Christian Bleitner: “At SGB, I have one fixed contact person. I do not know that from other suppliers.” Henning Wagner: “My personal SGB advisor takes care of everything.” (both translated)
Always “your SGB advisor”, never “our team”. One name, one number.
Straight
SGB's line “Ihre Energie, einfach besser.” (simply better). Gordon von Godin: “Transparent billing and personal contact are important to me.” (translated)
We say the uncomfortable part first: contracts renew when nobody acts, ours too. Then we say what SGB does about it.
Left out
SGB's pillars “KOSTEN MINIMIEREN / EINSPARUNGEN MAXIMIEREN”.
The voice never promises a saving. Section 1 gives no figure.

sections.title: The call before the date

fields.label: Summary
fields.text: An owner rarely chooses to stay with an energy supplier. The notice date passes during service, and the contract runs on. We show that trap first, because the owner is in it today, with another supplier. Then we show what SGB does about it: a personal advisor calls before every notice date, even SGB's own. That one service proves the whole offer: a person, not a call centre, who works for the owner. Every piece ends on one small ask: find out what SGB would cost you.

blocks.text: The evidence check

head: Question
What we found
Source
rows: Do business contracts renew when the owner misses the notice date?

Yes, as written. Since March 2022 a contract's standard terms may only let it roll on for an open term with one month's notice (BGB § 309 no. 9). That rule does not apply to terms used towards a business (BGB § 310 (1)). So a business contract may still add a full year. SGB's own Portfolio tariff renews by 12 months when nobody gives notice.
BGB § 309 no. 9 and § 310 (1), gesetze-im-internet.de (read 10 Nov 2026); Verbraucherzentrale, Marktcheck Kündigungsklauseln (read 10 Nov 2026); SGB news post, 5 Oct 2026 (ref 1.3)
Do owners miss it?

No survey of businesses answers this. We looked and found none. Three findings point the same way. One: before the law changed, a survey reported that a fifth of consumers held contracts they did not want, and one in four had trouble with automatic renewals. The law then closed the trap for households and left businesses in it. Two: two brokers for business energy warn of exactly this, and one writes that many businesses assume the household rule covers them. Three: in 2023, 14.6% of business supply points between 10 MWh and 2 GWh a year changed supplier, the band the regulator describes with restaurants as its first example. We keep the share of owners who missed a date as an assumption, and propose that SGB's advisors count it from week 1: [share of leads with an unchosen renewal].

Tagesspiegel, 16 Nov 2020 (headline and standfirst; the article is behind a paywall); wattline.de, Stromvertrag kündigen; energiehelden24.nrw, Gewerbestrom und Gewerbegas kündigen; Monitoringbericht 2024, Bundesnetzagentur and Bundeskartellamt (all read 10 Nov 2026)
Is there a second date owners miss?

Yes. When a supplier raises prices, a business may cancel without notice, but the supplier only has to tell a business two weeks ahead (a household: one month). A letter opened late closes that window too.
energiehelden24.nrw, Sonderkündigung (read 10 Nov 2026); a broker's guide, so it stays on our assumptions list until SGB confirms it
Why do owners hang up on energy calls?

Energy contracts are among the products most sold by cold call in Germany, and consumer advice centres report energy as the contract most often pushed on people after such calls. The Federal Network Agency can only fine cold calls to consumers; calls to businesses are not fined. So an owner hears from energy companies mostly when a stranger calls.
Bundesnetzagentur, Unerlaubte Telefonwerbung; Verbraucherzentrale, Achtung: Unerwünschte Energieverträge am Telefon (both read 10 Nov 2026)
Could another supplier sign the idea?

A reminder alone, yes: brokers already offer to note contract ends and remind. The twist, no. A broker is not the supplier, and we found no supplier that reminds a customer of its own notice date. So every piece carries “even SGB's own” right after the promise.
energiehelden24.nrw and Stromeus offer reminders (read 10 Nov 2026); the swap test

sections.eyebrow: Track A · our insight, our idea
sections.title: Meet your supplier

fields.label: Summary
fields.text: A restaurant runs on suppliers the owner knows by name. The butcher, the brewer and the wine merchant come to the door. Energy is one of the biggest bills on the desk, and it has no face: the energy people who call are strangers, and owners hang up. So we ask one question: ever met your energy supplier? At SGB the answer is yes. A personal advisor visits on site, handles the whole switch and stays the one contact. Every piece ends on one small ask: find out what SGB would cost you.

fields.label: Our insight, in one sentence
fields.text: Owners trust the suppliers they have met, and energy is the one big supplier they never meet.

fields.label: Our idea, in one sentence
fields.text: We ask owners if they have ever met their energy supplier, and show the SGB advisor who visits on site and handles the whole switch.

blocks.text: The research behind it

head: Finding
Source
What it means
rows: Energy contracts are among the products most sold by cold call in Germany, and calls to businesses cannot be fined by the regulator.
Bundesnetzagentur, Unerlaubte Telefonwerbung (read 10 Nov 2026)
The energy voice an owner knows is a stranger's voice on the phone.

Restaurants and hotels felt energy hardest: in a DEHOGA survey of 3,850 businesses (September 2022), energy costs rose 55% on average from October 2022 and 96% from January 2023. 48.8% of businesses then put energy at 10% of turnover or more.
DEHOGA via Meininger (2022); DEHOGA member survey via super44.ai (read 10 Nov 2026)
Energy is big and remembered. The cost is not the gap. The relationship is.
Most businesses stay where they are: in 2023, 14.6% of business supply points between 10 MWh and 2 GWh a year changed supplier. In 2024 the switching rate by volume was 14.1%.
Monitoringbericht 2024 and 2025, Bundesnetzagentur and Bundeskartellamt (read 10 Nov 2026)
In any one year, about six in seven stay. Staying is the default, not a choice made again.

Of the 13 customer quotes SGB gave us, four name the person first: one fixed contact person, “I do not know that from other suppliers” (Bleitner, translated), a personal advisor who takes care of everything (Wagner), personal care (Sagdic), personal contact (von Godin). Five name money.
SGB home page, appendix B

The proof is about a person. But competitors promise a personal advisor too (see the competitor scan under sources). So Track A stands on its execution, the supplier at the door, and not on the claim.
Owners distrust energy sales calls.
The brief's hypothesis; we found support for consumers, none measured for owners
We propose five short calls with owners from SGB's customer list before launch.

blocks.text: Two approaches we dropped

head: Approach
Why we dropped it
rows: The bill nobody reads: make the hidden energy cost of a kitchen visible, in the spirit of E.ON Italia's Floating Boat (appendix C).
It pulls every line toward a savings promise, which the brief rules out and section 1 cannot back with a figure. Any supplier could sign it.
Spot or fixed, explained: teach owners the price mix.
Every supplier explains its tariffs, so it fails the swap test. It also asks the most effort of the busiest owner. We kept it for the quiz, where the owner has already chosen to spend a minute.

blocks.text: Four-week test plan

head: Item
Our proposal
rows: What runs

Weeks 1 and 2: both tracks, cells A to F, on Meta (Facebook and Instagram, 4:5 and 9:16) and LinkedIn (4:5), with one audience: owners and managers of restaurants and hotels in Germany. Search runs on its own budget line, with the Track B promise. Week 3: the first stop and scale decisions. Week 4: scale the winners.
Budget split

Tracks 50/50, with the same daily caps. Within a track: A 20%, B 15%, C 20%, D 15%, E 15%, F 15%. Meta 80%, LinkedIn 20%: we doubt that many restaurant owners read LinkedIn, so it gets a small share and a hard check in week 2. Search sits outside the split.
Main metric
Cost per qualified lead for cells A to E. Cost per signed contract for cell F.
Lead status feedback

The advisor marks each lead qualified or not within two working days, in SGB's CRM. The status goes back daily as an offline conversion: Meta Conversions API, LinkedIn Conversions API, Google offline conversion import. So bidding learns from qualified leads, not from forms.
Decision rule

Week 3: stop a cell when its cost per qualified lead is more than 1.5 times the track's median, after at least [minimum leads per cell] leads. Never stop on clicks. Cell F is judged on signed contracts and gets all four weeks. Week 4: move the stopped budget to the best two cells of each track, and compare the tracks on cost per qualified lead at equal spend.
Weekly report

Per track and cell: spend, impressions, clicks, page visits, form starts, leads, qualified leads, cost per qualified lead, signed contracts (F), quiz starts, completed quizzes and contacts left (D), and the share of leads with an unchosen renewal.
What we would test first

Track B, cell A against cell C on Meta: the same headline, once with the page and once with the form inside the ad. It is the cheapest way to learn whether the twist earns a lead, and whether the page is worth its extra step.

blocks.text: Our own research

head: Finding
Source
rows: The 2022 rule against long automatic renewals protects consumers. It does not apply to terms used towards a business.
BGB § 309 no. 9 and § 310 (1), gesetze-im-internet.de
Before that law, a fifth of consumers held contracts they did not want, and one in four had trouble with automatic renewals.
Tagesspiegel, 16 November 2020 (headline and standfirst)
A business that misses the deadline gets an automatic renewal. Many businesses assume the household rule covers them.
wattline.de, Stromvertrag kündigen; energiehelden24.nrw, Gewerbestrom und Gewerbegas kündigen (two brokers, not research)
In 2023, 14.6% of business supply points between 10 MWh and 2 GWh a year changed supplier. In 2024 the switching rate of business customers by volume was 14.1%.
Monitoringbericht 2024 and Monitoringbericht 2025, Bundesnetzagentur and Bundeskartellamt
Energy contracts are among the products most sold by cold call. Only calls to consumers can be fined.
Bundesnetzagentur, Unerlaubte Telefonwerbung; Verbraucherzentrale, Achtung: Unerwünschte Energieverträge am Telefon
Energy costs of hospitality businesses rose 55% from October 2022 and 96% from January 2023 (3,850 businesses asked). 48.8% put energy at 10% of turnover or more.
DEHOGA survey, September 2022, via Meininger and via super44.ai
Brokers already offer contract reminders. We found no supplier that reminds customers of its own notice date, but we did not scan the whole market.
energiehelden24.nrw; our own reading, to be confirmed by SGB
HSBC UK fixed a hidden trap first, then showed people the trap.
The Homeless Bank Account, Cannes Lions 2021 (the brief's reference, appendix C)

head: Who
What they promise
What it means for us

items: “Your energy contract renews without you” is true for a contract with a renewal clause. The law allows it for businesses, and SGB's own Portfolio tariff has one. How many owners hold such a contract is not measured, so the body copy says “can renew”, never “most”.
[callback time]: SGB's callback time for a lead.
[advisor name], [region]: a real SGB advisor who agrees to appear, with written consent.
[weeks before]: how long before a notice date the advisor calls.
[booked time]: comes from the booking tool.
[share of leads with an unchosen renewal]: counted by the advisors from week 1. Until then, “owners miss the date” is supported, not measured.
[band 1] to [band 4]: monthly bill bands that separate small customers (SLP) from large ones (RLM). SGB sets them.
[minimum leads per cell]: the smallest count before a stop decision. It depends on the media budget, which the brief does not give.
[SGB's consent wording]: SGB gives the consent text for email and WhatsApp.
The three quiz fits (more fixed, more spot, a mix) are proposed. SGB has not confirmed them.
Cell B's offer, the bill check, is proposed. SGB has not confirmed it.
Owners distrust energy calls: the brief's hypothesis. We found it measured for consumers, not for owners.
The two-week notice of price changes to businesses comes from a broker's guide. SGB confirms or corrects it.
The field limits of Meta's and LinkedIn's instant forms are not checked. We check them in each platform before the build.
An owner who signs online may not have a named advisor yet. So cell F never promises one.
All photography is shot for SGB with real owners and advisors, with written consent. No actors pose as customers, and no generated people.

sections.title: What changed after the first review

head: In version 1
Why it failed
In version 2
rows: The headline was “We'll remind you when you can leave us.”
It spoke to someone who is already an SGB customer. The reader is a stranger, tied to another supplier. “Leave us” means nothing to them.
The headline shows the reader's own situation: “Your energy contract renews without you.”
The twist, “even SGB's own”, was the headline.
The twist is the proof, not the opening. Without the trap before it, nobody knows what it proves.
Trap first, then the promise, then the twist as its last three words.
Why SGB sat in the body copy.
The personal advisor, the price mix and the free switch are what SGB sells. They were not in a headline or a subline.
Every piece has a “why SGB” step, and the subline carries the personal advisor.
The ask was “ask for a callback”.
It named the mechanism, not what the owner gets from it.
One ask everywhere: “Find out what SGB would cost you.” The button then names the step.
Track A opened with “Butcher. Brewer. Your SGB advisor.”
A list is a riddle until you have read the subline.
A question the owner can answer at once: “Ever met your energy supplier?”

sections.title: Why, what we left out, what we test first

cards.title: Why these two ideas
cards.text: Track B: the owner is in the trap today, with another supplier, so we start there. The call before every notice date is a service SGB confirms, and “even SGB's own” is the part we found no other supplier saying. Track A: SGB's customers name a person before they name a price. Competitors claim a personal advisor too, so Track A stands on the on-site visit and on its execution. Track B is the stronger idea.

cards.title: What we left out
cards.text: Price and savings: five of SGB's quotes are about money, and we used none, because section 1 gives no figure. Sustainability. The tariff names. The 500 experts as a headline. A third idea about the bill, which we dropped. And every category picture: no bulbs, plugs or wind turbines.

cards.title: What we would test first
cards.text: Track B, cell A against cell C on Meta: the same hook and promise, once with the page and once with the form inside the ad. Then the trap headline against a headline that opens on the promise. The first number we want from SGB's advisors: how many new leads had a contract that renewed without a choice.

cards.title: What is not in this hand-in
cards.text: Work packages 2 and 3. The photography, which is shot for SGB with real people. German versions of the copy. The other four statics.

sections.title: From brief to copy
sections.lede: How this work was made. A language model writes. Code decides whether a line holds. A person decides what goes out. In this hand-in: 219 lines, 0 errors. 10 warnings are left open on the last page. 8 of them sit on lines that state SGB's promise in plain words, on purpose.

steps.title: Read the brief
steps.text: The brief becomes a brand file: 11 SGB facts with their source, 13 customer quotes word for word, every field limit, and what is ruled out.

steps.title: Research
steps.text: Law, regulator, trade body, competitors. Each finding keeps its source, or it becomes an assumption.

steps.title: Write
steps.text: A language model writes each line into its own field: headline, subline, button, script beat. It may only use facts from the brand file.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Code reads every line: the length of its field, quotes word for word, no number without a source, no price or saving, stock phrases, and the swap test.

steps.title: Send back
steps.text: A line that fails goes back to be rewritten. After the first review the copy went back as a whole: the reader had been misread, and no code check catches that. Section “What changed” shows it.

steps.title: A person decides
steps.text: A person reads the copy next to the report and decides what goes out. The Engine sends nothing on its own.

blocks.html: Next: every edit and every “no” becomes a lesson for the next brief. That part is built and not switched on yet. The full report of the check is on the last page.
